'''Mohammad Zahid Hasan''' (born 1971) is a Bangladeshi physicist and Eugene Higgins Professor of Physics at [[Princeton University]]. Hasan's research interests include [[quantum physics]] and [[quantum topology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Day |first=Charles |date=2009-04-01 |title=Exotic spin textures show up in diverse materials |url=https://physicstoday.aip.org/news/exotic-spin-textures-show-up-in-diverse-materials |journal=[[Physics Today]] |volume=62 |issue=4 |pages=12–13 |doi=10.1063/1.3120883|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and a fellow of the [[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellow Details: Dr. M. Zahid Hasan |url=https://www.bas.org.bd/fellow-details/137 |access-date=2026-07-05 |publisher=[[Bangladesh Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref>

==Personal life and career==
Born in [[Dhaka]], Bangladesh, in 1971,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. M. Zahid Hasan |url=https://mustafaprize.org/en/p/en-2036 |access-date=2024-10-19 |publisher=[[Mustafa Prize]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ahmed |first=Fakhruddin |date=2015-08-19 |title=BANGLADESH'S ZAHID HASAN |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/op-ed/bangladeshs-zahid-hasan-128782 |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |language=en}}</ref> Hasan attended [[Dhanmondi Government Boys' High School]], and later graduated from [[Dhaka College]] in 1988.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 25, 2024 |title=Bangladeshi scientist Zahid Hasan joins MIT as visiting professor |url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/people/344892/bangladeshi-scientist-zahid-hasan-becomes-visiting |access-date=2024-10-19 |work=[[Dhaka Tribune]]}}</ref> He was admitted to the physics department of [[Dhaka University]], but chose to attend the [[University of Texas at Austin]] on a scholarship.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chandan |first=Md. Shahnawaz Khan |date=March 17, 2017 |title=Zahid Hasan |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/star-weekend/zahid-hasan-1377007 |access-date=2024-10-19 |work=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]]}}</ref> Hasan completed his B.S. degree in physics, and then attended [[Stanford University]], from which he obtained an M.S. and a Ph.D.<ref>{{Cite web |title=M. Zahid Hasan |url=https://materials.princeton.edu/people/m-zahid-hasan |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=Princeton Materials Institute |publisher=[[Princeton University]] |language=en}}</ref>

Hasan's Ph.D. thesis, entitled ''Charge Dynamics in Low Dimensional Prototype Correlated Systems'', was published by the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] in November 2001 and by the [[Office of Scientific and Technical Information]] in March 2002. Advised by [[Zhi-Xun Shen]], the report served as Hasan's thesis in applied physics.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hasan |first=Md-Zahid |url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/11074749 |title=Charge Dynamics in Low Dimensional Prototype Correlated Systems: A View with High-Energy X-rays |date=2002 |doi=10.2172/799074 |osti=799074 |orig-date=2001}}</ref>

After his graduate work at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center and [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], Hasan became a Robert H. Dicke Fellow in fundamental physics at [[Princeton University]] and held appointments at [[Bell Laboratories]] and [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], before joining the faculty at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=M. Zahid Hasan |url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/m_zahid_hasan |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=[[Physics (magazine)|Physics]] |language=en}}</ref>

Hasan is the Principal Investigator of Laboratory for Topological Quantum Matter and Advanced Spectroscopy at Princeton University<ref name="knob">{{cite web|date=13 September 2018|title=Physicists find new control knob for the quantum topological world|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/physicists-find-new-control-knob-for-the-quantum-topological-world/|website=Physics World}}</ref> and a Visiting Faculty Scientist at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in California<ref name="LBNL">{{cite press release|title="How X-rays Pushed Topological Matter Research Over the Top" by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|website=lbl.gov|url=https://newscenter.lbl.gov/2017/04/14/how-x-rays-pushed-topological-matter-research-over-the-top/|date=14 April 2017|agency=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref> Since 2014 he has been an EPiQS-Moore Investigator, awarded by the Betty and [[Gordon Moore]] foundation in Palo Alto (California) for his research on emergent quantum phenomena in topological matter.<ref>{{citation|title="M. Zahid Hasan Experimental Investigator in Quantum Materials Award" by Moore foundation|date=2014|url=https://www.moore.org/grant-detail?grantId=GBMF4547|website=Betty and [[Gordon Moore]] foundation, Palo Alto, California}}</ref> He has been a Vanguard Fellow of the [[Aspen Institute]] (Washington DC) since 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Aspen Institute|url=https://www.aspeninstitute.org/|access-date=2020-04-24|website=The Aspen Institute|language=en-US}}</ref> Hasan is an elected fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Members Elected (2020): American Academy of Arts and Sciences|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2020|access-date=2020-04-23|website=Press Release by the American Academy of Arts & Sciences, Cambridge, Massachusetts, US|language=en}}</ref> In 2024, Hasan was appointed a visiting professor to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-25 |title=Bangladeshi scientist Zahid Hasan appointed visiting professor at MIT |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/tech-startup/news/bangladeshi-scientist-zahid-hasan-appointed-visiting-professor-mit-3595196 |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Hasan's research is focused on fundamental physics - either searching for, or in-depth exploration of novel phases of electronic quantum matter.<ref name="knob" /> He co-proposed and co-led the scattering-spectroscopy MERLIN beam-line and end-station facility at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kelez|first1=Nicholas|last2=Chuang|first2=Yi-De|last3=Smith-Baumann|first3=Alexis|last4=Franck|first4=Keith|last5=Duarte|first5=R.|last6=Lanzara|first6=A.|last7=Hasan|first7=M.Z.|last8=Dessau|first8=D.S.|last9=Chiang|first9=T.C.|last10=Shen|first10=Z.-X.|last11=Hussain|first11=Zahid|date=2007|title=Design of an elliptically bent refocus mirror for the MERLIN beamline at the advanced light source|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|language=en|volume=582|issue=1|pages=135–137|doi=10.1016/j.nima.2007.08.092|bibcode=2007NIMPA.582..135K}}</ref> and developed a laboratory for [[Ultrafast laser spectroscopy|ultrafast]] and [[Quantum coherence|coherent quantum]] phenomena at Princeton University.
